events.assessment: The customer reported transaction 3660153 as unauthorized. This transaction is part of a suspicious sequence of four identical $1800 online transactions (3660150, 3660151, 3660152, and 3660153) occurring within a six-day window, which represents a significant departure from the customer's historical baseline of mostly in-person transactions.
key_points: The flagged transaction 3660153 ($1800) is the fourth in a rapid succession of identical $1800 online transactions, following 3660150, 3660151, and 3660152.
While the first three $1800 transactions used billing address area 327.0, the disputed transaction 3660153 shifted to 315.0, matching the address area of an earlier in-person transaction 3652063.
The transaction model and bank risk scores remained low (model_p of 0.000657 and risk_score of 0.09 for 3660153), failing to flag this high-velocity, high-value burst.

key_points: Prior cases CC-4124, CC-4086, CC-3748, and CC-3907 established a pattern of unauthorized online purchases kept just under a $500 authorization threshold within a short timeframe.

events.claim: The transaction model, trained on the bank's own closed cases from July to October (its July-September version scored AUC 0.972 on October), scores this transaction 0.001, against a 2.0% base rate. It reads the unnamed Vesta C/D/M/V columns, the identity record, running aggregates of the resolved account and the graph's memory of earlier closed cases, all as known at transaction time. January activity is newer than anything the model learned from and carries patterns it has never seen, so a low score counts at most as weak evidence of innocence: its weight is bounded to between 0.5 and 8

7 online purchases between 2017-01-22 and 2017-01-31 climbing from $181.73 to $1,800.00 ($181.73 -> $357.82 -> $811.92 -> $1,800.00 -> $1,800.00 -> $1,800.00 -> $1,800.00), with 4 charges at the top amount: the pattern of someone probing the card's limit

The same escalating-value ramp signature appears on 13 other card(s) in the same 30 days: coordinated activity across customers, not one cardholder's habit; all of them on weaker evidence of their own, so they are monitored and not named here
